messages.content: Registration confirmed check-in by 10:00 Monday. That makes the early flight too exposed. Use the Sunday option and find me one practical downtown hotel for Sunday and Monday nights.

I agree with moving the outbound to Sunday, November 3. The nonstop leaves ORD at 6:20 p.m. and arrives at BNA at 7:55 p.m. The Tuesday return leaves BNA at 5:15 p.m. and reaches ORD at 7:05 p.m. The round-trip economy total is still $347.

For two nights downtown, the strongest fit is Hyatt Place Nashville Downtown. It is about a 10-minute walk from the workshop venue and roughly 15-25 minutes by rideshare from BNA in normal Sunday evening traffic. A king room is $612.84 total, including taxes and mandatory fees. Breakfast is included. Cancellation is free through 11:59 p.m. local time on Friday, November 1; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax.
Is there a less expensive downtown option that does not create a transportation problem?

The Holiday Inn & Suites Nashville Downtown - Broadway has a standard king room for $548.26 total for the same two nights. It is about a 15-minute walk from the venue, or a short rideshare if the weather is poor. The airport ride is comparable to the Hyatt Place. Breakfast is not included. Cancellation is free through 6:00 p.m. local time on Saturday, November 2; after that, one night plus tax is charged.
How do the full costs compare once breakfast and local transportation are considered?

Hyatt Place is $612.84 with breakfast included. Holiday Inn is $548.26, a difference of $64.58. Allowing roughly $20-$30 for two breakfasts, the Holiday Inn remains about $35-$45 less expensive. Airport rideshare costs should be effectively the same, and neither hotel requires a car. The Holiday Inn adds about five minutes of walking each way to the workshop.
Use the Holiday Inn. Before booking, make sure the Tuesday return is realistic after a 2:00 finish. I will have a checked bag stored at the hotel.

It is workable with a reasonable buffer. From the venue, allow 15 minutes to walk back to the hotel and another 10 minutes to retrieve the stored bag. Leaving the hotel around 2:30 p.m. should put you at BNA between 2:50 and 3:15 p.m., depending on traffic. That leaves about two hours before the 5:15 p.m. departure and at least 75 minutes before a typical checked-bag cutoff. I would not schedule anything after the workshop or delay departure from the hotel beyond 2:45 p.m.
What if the session runs fifteen minutes late?

A 2:15 p.m. finish still works. You should reach the hotel around 2:30, collect the bag, and leave by approximately 2:40. Even with a 30-minute ride, arrival at BNA would be around 3:10, just over two hours before departure. A longer overrun combined with unusually heavy traffic would start consuming the useful margin.
Good. Restate the flight times, hotel total, cancellation terms, and the Tuesday sequence in one place.

Outbound: Sunday, November 3, nonstop ORD-BNA, departing 6:20 p.m. and arriving 7:55 p.m. Return: Tuesday, November 5, nonstop BNA-ORD, departing 5:15 p.m. and arriving 7:05 p.m. Round-trip economy airfare: $347.00.

Hotel: Holiday Inn & Suites Nashville Downtown - Broadway, November 3-5, one standard king room for Marcus Lee. The complete two-night total is $548.26 including taxes and mandatory fees; breakfast is not included. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. Nashville time on Saturday, November 2. After that deadline, the penalty is one night plus tax.

Tuesday: workshop ends at 2:00 p.m.; walk to the hotel, retrieve the stored bag, and leave around 2:30 p.m. by rideshare. Expected BNA arrival is 2:50-3:15 p.m. for the 5:15 p.m. flight. The combined flight and hotel total is $895.26 before rideshares, meals, and any checked-bag charge.
Does the hotel confirm it will hold the bag after checkout?

Yes. The property confirms complimentary luggage storage for registered guests on the day of checkout. Storage is handled at the front desk and is subject to the usual claim-check procedure. Tuesday checkout is at 11:00 a.m., so you can leave the bag before going to the workshop and retrieve it afterward.
Book both. One traveler, Marcus Lee. Keep the checked bag out of the airfare total if it is paid separately.

I can complete the flight and hotel at the stated base totals. The airline fare is $347.00 for one traveler, and any checked-bag fee will remain separate. The hotel charge is $548.26 total. I am proceeding with the Sunday outbound, Tuesday return, and the two-night Holiday Inn stay.
Proceed.

The flight is confirmed for Marcus Lee under confirmation N4V7QC. Sunday’s nonstop leaves ORD at 6:20 p.m. and arrives at BNA at 7:55 p.m. Tuesday’s nonstop leaves BNA at 5:15 p.m. and arrives at ORD at 7:05 p.m. The airfare charged is $347.00; no checked bag has been prepaid.
And the hotel?

The Holiday Inn & Suites Nashville Downtown - Broadway is confirmed under hotel confirmation HIN-736204. The reservation is for November 3-5, one standard king room for Marcus Lee, at $548.26 total including taxes and mandatory fees. Breakfast is not included. Cancellation remains free through 6:00 p.m. Nashville time on November 2; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax.
Give me the arrival plan Sunday and the exact Tuesday transfer assumptions. I want those retained in case the agenda changes.

Sunday: after the 7:55 p.m. arrival at BNA, allow about 20-30 minutes to deplane and reach the rideshare pickup area if you do not check a bag, or additional time for baggage claim if you do. The rideshare to the Holiday Inn should take about 15-25 minutes in normal evening traffic, putting hotel arrival around 8:40-9:10 p.m.

Tuesday: check out by 11:00 a.m. and leave the bag with the front desk. With the workshop ending at 2:00 p.m., allow 15 minutes to walk back, 10 minutes to retrieve the bag, and depart the hotel by rideshare at about 2:30 p.m. The working drive estimate is 20-30 minutes, with a conservative airport arrival window of 2:50-3:15 p.m. for the 5:15 p.m. flight. A 2:15 p.m. finish remains feasible if you leave the hotel by roughly 2:40 p.m.; if the agenda moves later than that, the return should be reassessed.
